adjudication_records.issue_text: NewResourceServer hard-fails construction when search index initialization fails, turning per-request errors into process-level startup failures that prevent the Grafana server from starting

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly changes initialization from lazy per-request `s.Init(ctx)` calls (removed from Create/Update/Delete/Read/List/Watch/Search/etc.) to eager initialization during construction: `NewResourceServer` now calls `err := s.Init(ctx)` and returns `nil, err` on failure. Since `Init` runs `s.search.init(ctx)` and logs/retains `s.initErr`, any search index init error can now abort `NewResourceServer` creation, which plausibly can propagate to process startup failure if this constructor runs during startup. This is a real behavior/availability change, but the diff also contains a comment in `searchSupport.init` indicating failures are intended to block startup, so it’s not clearly a defect—more of an architectural/product decision to review.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Removing lazy Init() guards from non-search endpoints (Read, List, Create, Update, Delete, Watch) means a search-only failure now takes down all CRUD serving

adjudication.rationale: The diff makes `NewResourceServer` call `s.Init(ctx)` and return an error on failure (pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go), and `Init` runs `s.search.init(ctx)` when `s.search != nil`. Therefore a search-index init failure will prevent the server from being constructed and thus block all CRUD endpoints. However, this coupling already existed previously because CRUD endpoints called `s.Init(ctx)` themselves; the change is mainly that the failure now happens at startup instead of per-request. This is an architectural/behavioral concern rather than a clearly verifiable correctness bug from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Removing cacheMu.Lock() from the top of BuildIndex creates a concurrent bleve.New race on the same directory, causing lock/acquire errors or on-disk index corruption
getOrCreateIndex can build concurrently on cache eviction/rebuild on request paths, enabling races even with init-at-construction

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the coarse `cacheMu` lock that previously serialized `bleveBackend.BuildIndex` (`pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go`: deleted lock/unlock at start). Now the mutex only protects `b.cache[key] = idx`, meaning concurrent callers that miss the cache (e.g., via `getOrCreateIndex` after eviction/rebuild) can enter `BuildIndex` at the same time and attempt to create the same Bleve index (notably the same on-disk `dir` path when `size > FileThreshold`). That can lead to concurrent index creation conflicts/errors and/or inconsistent cache population. Moving `Init` to construction (`NewResourceServer` calling `s.Init`) doesn’t prevent later rebuilds, so the concurrency window remains.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Postgres integration test permanently skipped with a TODO, leaving TestIntegrationWillRunInstrumentationServerWhenTargetHasNoHttpServer with no database backend coverage in CI

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an unconditional skip for postgres in `TestIntegrationWillRunInstrumentationServerWhenTargetHasNoHttpServer` with a TODO (`if dbType == "postgres" { t.Skip(...) }`). Combined with the existing sqlite skip, this reduces/possibly eliminates CI coverage for that integration test on common DB backends. This is a concrete test-coverage regression introduced by the diff, though it’s not a product/runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: History and Origin methods call s.search.History/Origin unconditionally without a nil check, causing nil-interface panics when search is unconfigured, unlike Search which has an explicit nil check

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go, Search() explicitly checks `if s.search == nil { return nil, fmt.Errorf("search index not configured") }`, but History() and Origin() now directly do `return s.search.History(ctx, req)` / `return s.search.Origin(ctx, req)` with no nil guard. Since Init() only calls `s.search.init(ctx)` when `s.search != nil` and does not error when search is unconfigured, `s.search` can remain nil and these methods would panic on a nil pointer dereference.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Reordering initWatcher after search.init drops writes occurring during index build, leaving stale search results with no event captured

adjudication.rationale: The diff does reorder initialization in `server.Init`: it now calls `s.search.init(ctx)` before starting the watcher (`s.initWatcher()`), whereas previously the watcher started first. If `search.init` performs a potentially long index build, any writes/events occurring between the start of `search.init` and the later start of the watcher could be missed *unless* the watcher/reindex logic has a catch-up mechanism (not shown in this diff). The finding’s claim of definite dropped writes/stale results isn’t directly verifiable from the provided changes alone, but the ordering change does introduce a concrete race/consistency concern grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Only integration test covering the new eager-init startup path is skipped for postgres, leaving the changed startup behavior unverified in CI

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly adds a postgres skip to an integration test (`TestIntegrationWillRunInstrumentationServerWhenTargetHasNoHttpServer` in `pkg/server/module_server_test.go`), so when `dbType == "postgres"` the test will not execute in environments using postgres. That does reduce CI verification for whatever behavior this test covers. However, the claim that it is the *only* integration test covering the new eager-init startup path (introduced via `NewResourceServer` calling `s.Init(ctx)` in `pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go`) cannot be verified from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: History and Origin dereference s.search without a nil check while sibling Search handler retains one, causing nil-pointer panic when search is disabled

adjudication.rationale: In server.go, Search() explicitly guards `if s.search == nil { return nil, fmt.Errorf("search index not configured") }`, showing `s.search` can legitimately be nil. However, the diff changes History() and Origin() to directly call `s.search.History(ctx, req)` and `s.search.Origin(ctx, req)` with no nil check (and it also removed the prior `s.Init(ctx)` calls). If search is disabled/unconfigured (`s.search == nil`), History/Origin will panic with a nil-pointer dereference.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Narrowing cache mutex from whole build to cache write allows concurrent bleve.New calls on the same directory, causing file-lock build failures
Postgres integration test for storage server is broken and skipped with t.Skip and a TODO instead of being fixed, permanently losing postgres-path integration coverage

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly adds a TODO and a conditional `t.Skip` for `dbType == "postgres"` in `TestIntegrationWillRunInstrumentationServerWhenTargetHasNoHttpServerWhenTargetHasNoHttpServer` (pkg/server/module_server_test.go), with the message that it’s not working in Drone. This verifiably disables Postgres integration coverage for that test rather than fixing it, which is a real review concern but not a runtime product defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: NewResourceServer unconditionally calls Init in the constructor, changing the construction contract from lazy, recoverable per-request init to hard construction failure, breaking callers that tolerated transient init failures

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a concrete behavior change: `NewResourceServer` now calls `s.Init(ctx)` and returns an error on failure (added in `pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go`), while per-request `s.Init(ctx)` calls were removed from methods like `Create`, `Update`, `Delete`, `Read`, `List`, `Watch`, `Search`, etc. This clearly shifts initialization from lazy/per-request to eager/constructor-time. However, the claim that this "breaks callers that tolerated transient init failures" is not directly verifiable from the diff alone (we can't see callers or prior expectations), so it's best classified as an important contract/architecture concern grounded in the change, not a proven defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Per-request Init guards removed from all resource server methods, turning per-request retryable 500 failures into process-startup failures

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes `if err := s.Init(ctx); err != nil { ... }` guards from essentially all RPC handlers (Create/Update/Delete/Read/List/Watch/Search/History/Origin/IsHealthy/PutBlob/GetBlob) in `pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go` and instead calls `s.Init(ctx)` during construction in `NewResourceServer`, returning the error and preventing server creation. This is a real behavioral change: initialization failures that previously surfaced on first request (as handler errors) will now surface at startup/creation time. However, the claim that these were "retryable" per-request 500s isn’t directly supported by the diff (since `Init` uses `initOnce.Do`, failures are typically latched), so it’s more of an architectural/operational concern than a clearly verifiable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Public Init method remains on ResourceServer with internal call sites removed, so out-of-tree callers invoking Init after construction run a redundant second init with no test covering the double-init path

adjudication.rationale: The diff makes `NewResourceServer` call `s.Init(ctx)` before returning (pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go), and removes the per-RPC `s.Init(ctx)` calls from methods like Create/Update/Delete/Read/List/Watch/Search/etc. The exported `Init` method still exists, so any external (out-of-tree) code that previously did `srv := NewResourceServer(...); srv.Init(ctx)` would now call it a second time. The diff doesn’t show whether this is harmful (Init likely uses a once-guard, but that isn’t shown here), and the claim about missing test coverage for double-init isn’t directly verifiable from the diff, but the API/behavior change and potential redundant call pattern are real and diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Init reordering makes search index build run before initWatcher, creating a startup gap where writes during the build are missed by the watcher and silently omitted from the search index, causing stale search results

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly reorders initialization in `server.Init`: it now calls `s.search.init(ctx)` before `s.initWatcher()` (previously watcher started first). If the watcher is the mechanism that emits write events to keep the search index up to date, starting it after a potentially long index build could create a window where writes are not observed by the watcher. However, the diff does not show `initWatcher()`/event semantics (e.g., whether it can replay from a resource version), so the claim that writes are "silently omitted" and search results become stale is a plausible but not fully verifiable defect from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: BuildIndex no longer holds cacheMu across the build, making it safe only if the caller serializes per-key builds, but no guard, test, or comment establishes that invariant
matched_golden_ids: A race condition in BuildIndex allows multiple goroutines to concurrently build the same expensive index for the same key. This is caused by moving the b.cacheMu lock from protecting the entire function to only protecting the final cache assignment.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that BuildIndex no longer holds cacheMu during the build and warns that without per-key serialization multiple goroutines could run the expensive build concurrently. This is the same underlying race/duplicate-work issue described in the golden comment, caused by narrowing the lock to only the final cache assignment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Concurrent getOrCreateIndex calls for the same key can build two full bleve indexes concurrently, wasting memory/CPU and leaking the loser's open file index

adjudication.rationale: In `pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go`, `BuildIndex` used to hold `b.cacheMu` for the entire build (`b.cacheMu.Lock(); defer Unlock()`), but the diff removes that and now only locks around `b.cache[key] = idx`. This change allows multiple goroutines to concurrently execute the expensive `bleve.New(...)`/`bleve.NewMemOnly(...)` + `builder(...)` path for the same `key` before either stores into the cache. If that happens, the later store will overwrite the earlier `idx` in `b.cache` without any visible cleanup/close of the overwritten index in this diff, which matches the finding’s “duplicate full index build” and potential resource leak risk. (Whether `getOrCreateIndex` has additional per-key synchronization is not shown in the diff, so the issue is not fully provable here.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: initWatcher moved after search.init creates a window where writes during index build produce no WrittenEvent, leaving documents stale or missing from the search index

adjudication.rationale: The diff does reorder initialization in `server.Init`: it now runs `s.search.init(ctx)` before `s.initWatcher()` (see `pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go`), whereas previously the watcher was started first. If `initWatcher` is the mechanism that produces `WrittenEvent`s consumed by indexing, this reordering could create a gap during index build where concurrent writes wouldn’t be observed. However, the diff also changes behavior to call `s.Init(ctx)` inside `NewResourceServer` before returning the server, which likely reduces/avoids concurrent request writes during init. The diff alone doesn’t show whether writes can occur concurrently during init or whether the watcher can replay/catch up, so the “missing/stale documents” claim can’t be conclusively verified from the PR alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Init moved into NewResourceServer makes transient init failures a hard construction-time failure instead of lazy per-request degradation, affecting embedded servers and tests

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly changes initialization from lazy/per-request to construction-time: `NewResourceServer` now calls `s.Init(ctx)` and returns an error on failure (pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go), while all the previous `if err := s.Init(ctx); err != nil { ... }` guards were removed from request handlers (Create/Update/Delete/Read/List/Watch/Search/etc.). This makes any init failure prevent server construction entirely rather than surfacing as a per-request error, which can impact embedding and tests. Whether this is a defect depends on intended lifecycle semantics, so it’s a concrete design/behavior concern rather than a provable bug from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Full search-index build in the constructor blocks NewResourceServer for unbounded duration with no timeout

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `NewResourceServer` to synchronously call `s.Init(ctx)` before returning (`pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go`), and `Init` includes `s.search.init(ctx)` which performs search-index initialization/building during startup (commented as blocking continued execution). This means constructing the server can now take as long as index init takes, potentially delaying startup. The claim about “no timeout” isn’t directly verifiable from the diff because the origin/configuration of `ctx` in `NewResourceServer` isn’t shown, but the blocking-in-constructor concern is diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Removing cacheMu.Lock from BuildIndex allows two concurrent builds for the same key to both call bleve.New on the same directory path, corrupting the on-disk index

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go, BuildIndex previously held b.cacheMu for the entire function. The diff removes that lock and now only locks around `b.cache[key] = idx` at the end. This means two goroutines can concurrently execute BuildIndex for the same `key` and, when `size > b.opts.FileThreshold`, both can compute the same `dir := filepath.Join(...)` and call `bleve.New(dir, mapper)` concurrently. The diff shows no other per-key/in-progress guard around directory-backed index creation, so the change exposes a real race that can lead to conflicting writes/creation on the same on-disk index path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Concurrent builds race on the cache-set so the loser's index handle clobbers the winner's, serving the corrupted/abandoned index

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go, BuildIndex previously held b.cacheMu for the entire function (preventing concurrent builds for the same key). The diff removes that coarse lock and now only locks around `b.cache[key] = idx`. This allows two goroutines to concurrently build separate indexes for the same `key` and then race on the final cache assignment, where the last writer overwrites/clobbers the other index handle in the cache. The diff shows no guard (e.g., double-check, singleflight, compare-and-swap) to prevent this last-writer-wins behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Server initialization moved from lazy per-request to eager in constructor (NewResourceServer), turning retryable per-request init failures into hard startup failures without explicit acceptance or tests

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly moves initialization to be eager: `NewResourceServer` now calls `s.Init(ctx)` and returns an error if it fails (pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go), and all per-RPC `s.Init(ctx)` calls were removed from Create/Update/Delete/Read/List/Watch/Search/etc. This is a behavior/availability change: init failures now prevent server construction/startup rather than surfacing on first use. However, the finding’s claim that this removes “retryable per-request init failures” isn’t fully supported because `Init` uses `s.initOnce.Do(...)` and stores `s.initErr`, so prior per-request calls would not have retried initialization after a failure either. Still, making init a hard startup requirement is a significant change that warrants explicit acceptance/tests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: initWatcher() reordered to run after search index build, so writes committed between index build and watcher start are never delivered, permanently staling the in-memory search index

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly reorders initialization in `server.Init`: it now calls `s.search.init(ctx)` (search index build) before `s.initWatcher()` (watching for changes), whereas previously the watcher started first. This change can create a window where resource writes occurring during index initialization might not be observed by the watcher depending on how `initWatcher()` seeds/streams events. However, the diff does not show `initWatcher()`’s semantics (e.g., whether it replays from a known RV), so the claim of “never delivered, permanently staling” cannot be conclusively verified from the provided changes alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Postgres integration test permanently skipped with t.Skip and TODO, leaving the PR's riskiest changes untested against the production database

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly adds a Postgres-specific skip in `TestIntegrationWillRunInstrumentationServerWhenTargetHasNoHttpServerWhenTargetHasNoHttpServer` (in `pkg/server/module_server_test.go`): `// TODO - fix this test for postgres` followed by `if dbType == "postgres" { t.Skip("skipping - test not working with postgres in Drone. Works locally.") }`. This means the integration test will not run under Postgres in CI, reducing coverage for changes that may affect the production DB path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Moving Init(ctx) from per-request lazy init into NewResourceServer converts per-request failures into hard startup failures, causing full server unavailability if any Init component (e.g., search index build) fails

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly moves initialization from lazy per-request checks to constructor-time: `NewResourceServer` now calls `err := s.Init(ctx)` and returns an error if it fails, while all prior `if err := s.Init(ctx); err != nil { ... }` blocks were removed from request handlers (Create/Update/Delete/Read/List/Watch/Search/etc.). This does convert any `Init` failure (including `s.search.init(ctx)` when `s.search != nil`) into a hard failure to construct the server, which can make the whole server unavailable rather than failing individual requests. Whether this is a defect or intended "fail fast" behavior isn’t provable from the diff alone, but it is a concrete, impactful behavior/availability change worth calling out.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Removal of lazy init is unconditional with no flag to opt back into degraded-capacity operation

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes per-request lazy initialization (`if err := s.Init(ctx); err != nil { ... }`) from many RPC handlers (Create/Update/Delete/Read/List/Watch/Search/History/Origin/IsHealthy/PutBlob/GetBlob) and instead calls `s.Init(ctx)` unconditionally during `NewResourceServer` construction, returning an error if init fails. This is a real behavior/operational change (startup now hard-fails instead of potentially serving some functionality before/without full init), and the diff shows no configuration/flag to preserve the prior lazy/degraded behavior. Whether that degraded mode is required isn’t provable from the diff alone, so it’s not a verifiable bug, but it is a concrete review concern created by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Reordering of initWatcher after s.search.init (server.go:303–310) is a race/correctness concern

adjudication.rationale: The diff does reorder initialization in server.Init: it now runs `s.search.init(ctx)` before `s.initWatcher()` (previously watcher started first). That creates a new behavioral window where external resource changes could occur while the search index is being built but before the watcher starts, potentially leaving the index out-of-date depending on how `initWatcher()` establishes its starting point (not shown in the diff). This is a specific, diff-grounded ordering concern, but the diff alone doesn’t prove it’s a definite bug without seeing watcher semantics.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Lock re-scoping in bleve.go:85–140 is a race/correctness concern

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go BuildIndex, the diff removes holding b.cacheMu for the entire function and now only locks around `b.cache[key] = idx`. This means multiple goroutines can concurrently execute the expensive index creation/build path for the same `key` (including `bleve.New(dir, mapper)` for file-backed indexes using the same `dir`), which can lead to concurrent creation/use of the same on-disk index directory and/or duplicate builds with last-writer-wins cache population. The old wider lock prevented these concurrent builds; the new scoping only protects the map write, not the correctness of the build process.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Only integration test exercising the server lifecycle is skipped via postgres t.Skip, leaving the new eager Init constructor behavior untested in CI

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new `t.Skip` for `dbType == "postgres"` in `TestIntegrationWillRunInstrumentationServerWhenTargetHasNoHttpServer` (module_server_test.go), explicitly disabling that integration test under Postgres CI. At the same time, `NewResourceServer` now eagerly calls `s.Init(ctx)` and per-RPC `Init` calls were removed (server.go). Skipping this integration test on Postgres plausibly reduces CI coverage for the new eager-init/server-lifecycle behavior on that backend. However, the claim that this is the *only* integration test covering lifecycle cannot be verified from the provided diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Removed pre-build lock in bleve.go BuildIndex introduces a concurrent-build race where two getOrCreateIndex calls for the same NamespacedResource both call bleve.New on the same directory, causing lock/file-in-use errors or leaked index handles

adjudication.rationale: In `pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go` the `BuildIndex` method removed the `cacheMu` lock that previously wrapped the entire build path (including the `bleve.New(dir, ...)` / `bleve.NewMemOnly(...)` creation). The only remaining locking is around `b.cache[key] = idx`. This means two concurrent `BuildIndex` calls for the same `key` can both proceed past cache-miss logic (not shown here) and attempt to create/open the same on-disk index directory (`dir := filepath.Join(...)`), leading to create/open conflicts (e.g., "already exists" / file-in-use) and/or leaking one of the created index handles (the later write overwrites the cache entry). The diff does not add any per-key build synchronization to replace the removed lock.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No test asserts that a failing search init (e.g., bad index directory) causes NewResourceServer to return an error rather than a half-initialized server

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds eager initialization in `NewResourceServer` (`err := s.Init(ctx)` then return error) and removes per-RPC `Init` calls, but it does not show the full test suite. From this PR diff alone we cannot verify the claim that *no test* asserts `NewResourceServer` errors on a failing search init (such a test could exist elsewhere outside the shown hunks). adjudication_records.issue_text: Init moved from lazy per-request to hard construction-time failure in pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go:255-260, converting a previously recoverable per-pod condition into a startup crash that can crash-loop pods on transient init failures during rolling deploys

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly changes initialization semantics: `NewResourceServer` now calls `s.Init(ctx)` and returns an error on failure (server.go around the added block after construction), and all per-request `if err := s.Init(ctx); err != nil { ... }` checks were removed from methods like `Create/Update/Delete/Read/List/Watch/Search/...`. This makes init failures surface at construction/startup instead of being deferred until first request, which can indeed turn a previously lazy/possibly recoverable condition into a hard startup failure depending on how `NewResourceServer` errors are handled by the caller (not shown in this diff).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Init ordering swap in pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go:294-311 (search init before watcher) can index a stale snapshot and miss concurrent writes, causing search results to silently omit recently-written resources if the watcher's start RV is 'now' rather than 'index build start'

adjudication.rationale: The diff in pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go does swap initialization order: it now calls `s.search.init(ctx)` before `s.initWatcher()` (lines ~300-311). That change could create a window where writes occur after the search index snapshot/build starts but before the watcher begins consuming events. Whether those writes are actually missed depends on how `initWatcher()` chooses its starting resource version (e.g., “now” vs “from beginning/last RV”), which is not shown in this diff, so the claimed silent omission isn’t directly verifiable here. Still, the ordering change is real and the potential gap is a concrete, diff-grounded concern to review.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Init errors checked only at construction in NewResourceServer, but init runs in a background goroutine so the check passes before s.initErr is set, and removed per-RPC checks mean all RPCs silently serve against uninitialized backends

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows NewResourceServer now calls `s.Init(ctx)` synchronously and returns an error immediately if Init fails (`err := s.Init(ctx); if err != nil { ...; return nil, err }`). In `server.Init`, initialization work (`s.search.init(ctx)` and `s.initWatcher()`) is executed inside `s.initOnce.Do(...)` before `Init` returns; the snippet does not show Init delegating initialization to a background goroutine or setting `s.initErr` asynchronously. adjudication_records.issue_text: History/Origin RPC paths can panic on nil s.search since they lack the s.search == nil guard present in Search

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go, Search explicitly guards `if s.search == nil { return nil, fmt.Errorf("search index not configured") }`, showing `s.search` can be nil. However, History and Origin now directly call `s.search.History(ctx, req)` and `s.search.Origin(ctx, req)` with no nil check (and the prior `s.Init(ctx)` calls were removed), so if `s.search` is nil these RPC handlers will dereference nil and panic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dropping cacheMu for the duration of BuildIndex allows concurrent bleve.New calls on the same directory, causing 'index path already contains an index' errors and cache overwrites of in-use index handles

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go, BuildIndex previously held b.cacheMu for the entire function (lock+defer unlock). The diff removes that and now only locks around `b.cache[key] = idx`. That means two concurrent BuildIndex calls for the same `key` can both reach `bleve.New(dir, mapper)` for the same on-disk `dir` (when `size > b.opts.FileThreshold`), which can race and fail with directory-already-has-index type errors and/or lead to last-writer-wins overwriting `b.cache[key]` while another handle is in use. The diff shows no other synchronization guarding index creation per key.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Moving init into the constructor converts per-request failures into hard process startup failures, causing crash-loops on transient boot-time dependency issues

adjudication.rationale: The diff moves initialization to construction: `NewResourceServer` now calls `err := s.Init(ctx)` and returns an error on failure, while per-request calls to `s.Init(ctx)` were removed from `Create/Update/Delete/Read/List/Watch/Search/...` (multiple deletions shown). This is a concrete behavior change from lazy/per-request init failures to startup-time failure, which can indeed make transient dependency problems prevent the server from starting (potentially causing restart loops) rather than only failing the first request. Whether that’s desired is an architectural/operational concern, not an inherently verifiable correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The 'search index initialized' log line executes immediately after spawning the build goroutine, reporting duration_secs ~0 and wrong total_docs, misleading operators

adjudication.rationale: In `pkg/storage/unified/resource/search.go` `(*searchSupport).init`, the code starts a goroutine (`go func() { ... }()`) and then immediately computes `end := time.Now().Unix()` and logs `s.log.Info("search index initialized", "duration_secs", end-start, "total_docs", s.search.TotalDocs())`. There is no wait/join/synchronization shown before this log, so the message can be emitted before the background build work completes, making `duration_secs` near-zero and `total_docs` potentially not representative yet. This is misleading observability rather than a functional correctness failure shown by the diff.
